I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive

Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of  great games that are very clear and understandable
In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks

And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends.
Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy

And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights
Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points

If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else
With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

I have played more than 25 hours of this game and still have lot of content left to discover. It is one of the best roguelite games of all time with crisp combat and funny parodies of other legendary 2D games like Hollow Knight, Katana Zero etc. Apart from the gorgeous pixel-art, the game has amazing soundtracks and the level design is one of the best I have seen in 2D games. 

No single run is same, you keep discovering new weapons, abilities etc. and the game has quite a few challenging bosses. The game is somewhat on the difficult side, though you keep unlocking stuff it does take time if you are not good with combat. I played the game with all the DLCs installed so I don't know what the game is like without the DLCs but the base game itself is massive from what I have seen.

For the price and level of replayability, I would highly recommend it even at the base price but it does come on sale frequently.
Tight gameplay, exploration / secrets, and razor-sharp controls make Dead Cells one of the absolute best 2D action-roguelites ever created.

Is this a bad game? Maybe not objectively. Graphics style is cool, the controls feel fast and responsive, and it's got a whole lot of content. Music is manageable, but not memorable.

But am I having fun playing this? To be honest, not particularly. It's a combination of things. Just to ramble a bit:
- The game is designed to be grindy by design. You have to unlock every f--ing thing. If that's what keeps if interesting for you, sure. Otherwise: eh. It's really one big grind-a-thon, The roguelite genre taken to extremes.
- There may be a story somewhere, but i was just some headless dude fighting through dungeons until i killed a king. And then I was back at the start. Some vague lore drops are dropped here and there, but i didn't really care about it since it was never presented in a way that made me care. Or something. 
- Then you traverse a whole corridor only to find out you don't have the permanent upgrade unlocked that is required to keep going that way. Or worse, it leads to a door and when you try to enter it it says "DLC REQUIRED". Please.
- Partly a skill issue, but the combat system never really clicked for me either. When going 1 on 1, it's usually okay, but when it gets more frenzied a lot of stuff can be going on at the screen especially with gibs and effects. This can lead to bs like (for example) make it hard to see enemy projectiles. 

At the end of it all, the core gameplay loop doesn't seem to reward much other than feeding into itself for the sake of it. And I never really had that "just one more try" moment that some games give. I might throw a few more runs in after this review. But I don't expect it to cause me to drastically change my opinion from this.
Little did I know, that I was playing the new Castlevania without knowing. The french were training me to accept a new Dead Cells with another coat of paint.

A masterclass in blending roguelite and Metroidvania into something that feels both fresh and endlessly replayable. The combat is the star here: fast, fluid, and brutally satisfying, with every dodge, parry, and weapon combination feeling weighty and responsive . The pixel art is gorgeous, the soundtrack slaps, and the progression system—unlocking new weapons and permanent upgrades between runs—keeps you coming back even after a hundred deaths .

The caveats are real: it's punishing, and the difficulty curve after the first clear is a genuine wall that demands patience and practice . Some weapons feel unbalanced, and the early biomes can get repetitive after dozens of hours . But with 97% positive Steam reviews from over 130,000 players and multiple Game of the Year awards, this is essential for anyone who loves action games that respect your skill . Just be ready to die. A lot.

If you arent critical of Rougelikes as a genre, youll probably enjoy this game quite a bit. It has a lot going for it. Fun combat, endless unlocks, and good replayability

If you're like me, and critical of Rougelikes, you'll also feel like this game controls like a floaty platformer mobile game. That is because this is a floaty mobile game. Button presses such as attacks aren't very satisfying, and movement/platforming is very floatly

There's some stuff to like, its a decent game, but there's millions of better rougelikes. This would have objectively been a better game if it didn't have to compromise its gamefeel/controls just to be a mobile game, but that isn't the Dead Cells we got

I bought this on release, played it for a bit, then dumped it after 5 hours.
Two years later, I picked up Hades, played it for a bit, and promptly dumped it after 5 hours.

Then randomly, about a year ago, I decided to pick up Hades again, played it for a bit... and I finally "got" it, I "got" the roguelite loop, got addicted and went on a massive roguelite binge that's lasted until now.

So, 8 years later, I'm finally revisiting Dead Cells. Full circle moment.

It's great. It's addicting. I love it some times, and I hate it some times.
I have a love-hate relationship with this one.

Hades, love it.
BlazBlue, love it.
Trinity Fusion, love it.
Oblivion Override, love it.

This one? I lovehate it.
It's an abusive relationship, where the roles swap back and forth.
Once I'm kinda done with this one, I think I can finally lay roguelites to rest for a bit, and go back to Soulslikes and RPGs again.

But, for now, still got some game here and some explosive barrels to get clipped by in the distillery!
